utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I understand the video-conferencing equipment in Dubrovnik is to some limited degree damaged. Therefore, it's not possible to have the videolink at the moment with the witness General Marinovic. He was spoken to yesterday by telephone in my presence and is fit and prepared to give evidence. I'm informed that Registry staff in Dubrovnik are pursuing an alternative set of equipment in Dubrovnik with the hope of being able to start today. In those circumstances, may we proceed with another witness, who's a protected witness, but on the basis that if the video-conferencing equipment becomes available, we should stop that witness and take the opportunity to have the evidence of General Marinovic today, if at all possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we shouldn't clearly waste time. It's not satisfactory that the order of witnesses is changed, but this, one understands, is beyond the controls of the Prosecution. So the proposal is that we take this next witness who we have the details here. He was on the list, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Oh, certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He was the next one on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm informed, incidentally, that the Sarajevo video-conferencing equipment is separate from the travelling equipment and is therefore likely to be functioning whatever the outcome of today's efforts may be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So we can take -- how long is this current witness -- this proposed new witness likely to be in chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's said by Mr. Groome about an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Hour and a half. So we could hear this witness and then review the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Hear him in chief, maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think from the figure of the general as revealed on the telephone yesterday, he will certainly be capable of answering questions for an hour. He may well be, as was indicated in earlier applications, willing and able to go a little longer than that, so it would be wise to make the maximum possible use today of any video-conferencing time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the subject of witnesses, to give the earliest advanced notice, a witness listed for this week was B-97. I do not intend to call that witness so that there may be further advancing of witnesses or substitution of witnesses to fill that gap, especially if the gap is enlarged by the inability to call General Marinovic today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The other issue is, I should tell you, that we ought to go on with, at some stage, with the Rule 92 bis proposed witnesses and also the transcripts in the Croatia case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We agree and we thought about that at our discussions this morning, but of course Mr. Kay isn't here today. So that if we can't do video-conferencing and if we finish this witness, and there's no reason to extend the witness simply because there is time available, then there may come a time at the end of today when we could be pushed to find something to fill the time, but I'll do my best to ensure that we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well, we'll hear the witness in chief and then review the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls Prosecution witness B-1738. I would note for the Chamber that this witness, pursuant to an order from the Chamber, has been granted voice and facial distortion as well as a pseudonym. There will be one new binder of exhibits, and it would be possible to have a number assigned at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next number will be P411.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if I might note for the Chamber, tab 4 in your binders is empty. Because the witness has been accelerated, that exhibit was not available at this moment. It will be available in an hour or two. I will be requesting leave to put that -- it's a photograph, to put that photograph to the witness on re-examination if it is not available before I conclude my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that we begin by showing the witness Prosecution Exhibit 411, tab 1. This is an exhibit we will be tendering under seal so I would ask that it not be placed on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask you to take a look at that document, and first I would ask you, is that your name on the first line of the table that's indicated on that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is that your date of birth directly under your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I've finished with the exhibit. I would note for the Chamber that in order to attempt to have as much of this testimony in open session, the witness will refer to several locations and people by the terms listed on this document rather than the actual location or the actual name of the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to begin your testimony this morning by describing for the Chamber, briefly, your educational background.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I have completed eight years of elementary school and three years of secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In your secondary school, how many different subjects did you study?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Two streams of subjects.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe the first subject that you studied and whether or not you completed your course of study in that particular area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: The first was the police section, which I did not complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why did you not complete your studies in the police field?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I had some problems on an ethnic basis, and I got into a fight with several fellow pupils who were Croats by ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what is your ethnicity, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After not completing your police studies, did you then move on to another pursuit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I continued in a school for truck drivers in my own town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was the town that you were -- you grew up in and attended school, was that in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you left Croatia and went to stay with your grandmother who lived in a place in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. That was at the beginning of the summer of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And why is it that you left Croatia and went to live with your grandmother in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Once again, I had problems on an ethnic basis in my town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe what, if any -- what was the situation in the village in which your grandmother lived, what was the situation between the different ethnic groups in Bosnia at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you returned to your hometown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes; at the beginning of September of that same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe the relationship or the conditions between the different ethnic groups in your hometown in Croatia when you returned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: The situation was difficult, and there was shooting too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Because of the situation as you found it when you returned, did you go stay in a place that you thought offered you some measure of safety?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us where it was you stayed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I went to the barracks of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did you remain at the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: About two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While there, were you assigned tasks to complete by members of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: To cooperate with the army and to defend the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you consider yourself to have officially enlisted in the Yugoslav People's Army during this time that you were at the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While you were in the barracks, did it come to pass that the barracks was attacked by Croat forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, on three occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you give the Chamber some indication of the severity of the attacks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Larger or smaller groups of armed civilians shot at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you left the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. I left sometime in November of that same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you leave in response to or at the time of the third attack on the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And it was agreed that the Croatian authorities should release us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Without telling us the specific location of where you went, can you tell us how far away was the location that you went to from the barracks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: About 25 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On your way or during the time that you were leaving the barracks, did something happen between yourself and a Croat man with a gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: One of the Croats recognised me, and they thought that I was a volunteer. One of them wanted to kill me, and he placed a gun into my mouth. And they beat me up a bit. And their commander said that the agreement was that everybody who was alive had to leave town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that you went to a place about 25 kilometres from the barracks. How long did you remain at that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Between 10 and 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you go after leaving that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Once again to Bosnia, to my grandmother's.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was your purpose for going there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I went there to find my closest family members because I didn't know where they were actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you arrived at your grandmother's village, did you discover where your immediate family was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Nobody knew anything about their whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not finding your family there, did you go somewhere else in an attempt to find them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I went to Serbia, to my uncle's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you find them there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time while at your uncle's house that you learnt that somebody was looking for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, and it was the military police, in fact, of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you do when you learnt of this fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I went to another town to stay with a friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the friend that you went to stay with, would I be correct in saying that it was in the vicinity of Belgrade in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you responded to a television advertisement by Arkan for Arkan's Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I saw it -- an advertisement, a recruiting advertisement on television, and I asked around to see what it was about and decided to apply.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber what you recall about the television advertisement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but they showed Arkan with a tiger. There were several soldiers with him, and they said a little bit about the kind of training we would undergo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What is your best memory regarding what time or what date you see this advertisement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: It was in January 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've testified that you asked around for more information regarding Arkan's Tigers. Did you learn or were you told what the pay was for recruits to the Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I learned from friends that one could sign a contract for three, six, or 12 months, and that the pay was 400 German marks a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you consider that to be good pay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: In those days, it was rather good.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you also learn that by serving as a member of Arkan's Tigers you could satisfy your requirement for serving in the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. That was also one of the reasons why I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you said you went there, can you tell us where it was that you went to enlist with Arkan's Tigers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: To Arkan's office close to the Red Star stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was that in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber what you observed when you arrived at Arkan's office.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: In front of the office there were two armed men in civilian clothing. They stopped me and asked me what I wanted. I said I wanted to enroll. And regarding two of my friends who had brought me there and who did not want to enlist, they told them to go away. I entered the office. A man was inside who took down my particulars and said I would have to wait for Arkan himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when Arkan himself arrived at the office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: About half an hour later he arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have a conversation with Arkan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, I talked to him, and at first he said I was too young, but as I had had some wartime experience, he agreed to accept me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he ask you to sign a contract?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I signed a contract for a three-month period.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber what, if anything, you recall about the terms of that contract.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I just remember that my particulars were noted and that it covered a period of three months.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to signing this contract and agreeing to enter Arkan's Tigers, had you at any time been a member of his political party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber what occurred after you signed this contract.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I went to his ice cream parlor and waited for transportation to take me to Erdut. In the meantime, I met one of Arkan's bodyguards. And talking to him, I learnt that there would be no pay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there other recruits that you met that day in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: That day another two arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you eventually go to Erdut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you go to Erdut the same day that you went to Arkan's office for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you get to Erdut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: One of Arkan's drivers drove us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber what you observed when you arrived at Erdut.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: The place looked like a military barracks. It was -- it had a wire fence around it and several buildings inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe what, if any, people you observed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: There were perhaps several. Actually, they were all in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you approximate the number of people that you saw at the camp when you arrived that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: During the line-up for supper, there were about 150 of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've described for the Chamber that you saw the advertisement in January of 1992. Can you approximate for us, when is it that you arrive at Erdut camp for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: At the beginning of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long were you engaged or did you remain at Erdut at that time before you were deployed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Just under two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to describe for the Chamber the names of any of the members of Arkan's Tigers that appeared to you to have a position of authority within the organisation and the camp at Erdut.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: The two leading ones had nicknames of Peja and Puki.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are there others that were there that came underneath these two leading men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. There were quite a number of officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us any of the names that you can recall today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Among the senior officers, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At the camp, did the people present at the camp use their legal names or did they use nicknames?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: We mostly used our nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you at this time, would you describe to the Chamber the types of training that was generally given to recruits at the Erdut camp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: The training was in discipline with a lot of running and training in the use of all types of firearms and explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At what point during the course of the training were recruits issued a firearm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: The recruits were issued a firearm as soon as they arrived at the centre, and they had a weapon with them throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber the training camp at Erdut. How far away is it from the nearest populated area or houses? Can you give the Chamber some idea about where it was in respect to other locations in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Erdut was an inhabited place, a settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You testified that it was surrounded -- the training camp was surrounded by a fence. Was it possible to look out of the fence and see traffic passing by and people passing by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. And most of the time regarding the running, actually we ran outside the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you -- would it have been possible for somebody on the outside of the camp looking inside the camp to see you and the other recruits carrying your weapons and engaging -- engaged in training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: In those days, anyone could see because fence was a wire fence, and you could easily look through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the times that you ran outside the camp facility, during any of those occasions were -- did the men carry their weapons with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: At all times; during the day and the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You spoke about training and discipline. Was there an occasion in which a member, a fellow recruit, received harsh discipline for drinking alcohol during the training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. He was caught drunk on guard duty, and he was tied to a flagpole and he was beaten with some kind of a stick, baton.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The recruits, were the recruits issued a standard uniform that they all were required to wear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. All were dressed in the same manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe the uniform to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: In those days, it was in one piece like an overall. It was greyish-green in colour with the emblems on the sleeves. The caps were green berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were recruits --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Or -- or black caps which you pull over, over your face like a mask.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On the uniform that you're describing, were there any patches to identify those wearing the uniform as members of Arkan's Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. There was the emblem of the Serbian Volunteer Guards and an emblem with a tiger.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You just said Serbian Volunteer Guards. Was that the official name that Arkan's Tigers were known as?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: One of the two official names.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at the television screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I'd ask that perhaps the usher would switch it to off, so we will use the Sanction system. This would be tabs 2 through 5 in Prosecution Exhibit 411 and will also be displayed on the computer monitors for those and the Chamber who would like to -- my apologies. Your Honour, with an earlier witness we began a patch book that is Prosecution Exhibit 349. We are proposing to add these additional patches as tabs 2 through 5 into that prior exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to look at the computer monitor in front of you. Do you recognise that patch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. That is the patch of Arkan's guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that similar to the patch that you wore on your uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, only I'm not sure whether it was like this or whether it had the background in black.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at the next exhibit, and this would be Prosecution 349, tab 3. Do you recognise this patch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. That is also the patch that is the same as the previous one, only the background is in a different colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at another patch. That would be Prosecution Exhibit 349, tab 4. I'd ask you if you recognise this patch.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. That also is the emblem of Arkan's Tigers, which was attached on other side of the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I will ask you about Mauzer's Panther unit in greater detail later in your testimony, but I'm going to ask you to look at one final patch and ask you if you recognise this patch. It's Prosecution Exhibit 349, tab 5.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, it is the patch of the so-called Serbian National Guards under the command of Mauzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you and a number of other recruits were deployed for the first time out of Erdut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please tell us when that was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: On the 31st of March, 1992, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe the circumstances surrounding how you learned that you were being deployed on a particular mission.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Late in the evening, we had an alert and a line-up outside, and later, Arkan selected 45 members for an operation, and I was one of those selected.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you told where you were going to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No. None of us knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there rumours among the men regarding where you might be going to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. We discussed the possibility of going to Mostar amongst ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to leaving Erdut, were the men, the 45 men that were selected, were they issued with any additional equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: That same evening, we received each two hand grenades and two hand-held rocket launchers known as Zoljas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately what time of the day did you leave Erdut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Around 2.00 or 3.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber as best you can remember the path -- I'm sorry. I withdraw that question. How did you leave Erdut? In what type of vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: We set off by bus, escorted by one or two jeeps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And best as you can recall, can you describe the journey or the path that the bus took.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: We crossed the border at Erdut into Serbia, and we travelled through Serbia up to a small frontier crossing into Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber what locations in Serbia the bus passed through?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I slept most of the journey, but I know for sure that we passed through Odzaci, Backa Palanka, Badovinci.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the times that you were awake during this journey, would you be able to characterise for the Chamber the type of road you were on; were you on a primary road, a secondary road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Normal roads used for public transport.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, when you crossed from Croatia into Serbia, were there border controls on the Serbian side of that border?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: There were no controls.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you travelled from Serbia into Bosnia, were there any border controls at that crossing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you go in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: We crossed the Drina to the Popovi village not far from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you cross the Drina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: With a ferry that ferries cars. This was a public crossing point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived in Popovi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: We met up with several members of Arkan's Guards and a number of armed civilians, that is, local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how long did you remain at Popovi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Not long.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you go when you left Popovi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: To Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did the local Serbs that you saw in Popovi, did they go with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to return for a moment at the -- to the ferry crossing. Were there any members of the police or military on the Serbian side of the ferry crossing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How about on the Bosnian side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, there were some police there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the police on the Bosnian side stop the bus and check the identities of yourself or any of the other men that were travelling into Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When did you learn that you were going to Bijeljina for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I learnt when I got off the bus at Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where in the municipality of Bijeljina did you get off the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: A kilometre or a kilometre and a half away from the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness now be shown Prosecution Exhibit 411, tab 2. I'd ask that it be placed on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to take -- first let me ask you this: Do you recognise what's on the overhead projector to your left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. It is a map showing the route from Erdut to Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that a map that you drew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to take the pointer, indicate Erdut, the place where you started, and then just trace for the Chamber the path, as best you recall, that you took to Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: From Erdut via a place called Odzaci, Backa Palanka, and finally, the crossing close to Badovinci, the crossing over the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would now ask that another map - and this would be an enlarged copy of Prosecution Exhibit 326, page 29 - I'd ask that that be placed on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: That is the border crossing between Badovinci and Popovo. It is the place of Popovi where we met up with the rest of the group. And there is Bijeljina, where there was a conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is there -- did you also -- did you circle the locations on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you, for the sake of saving some time, can you point to the location of Janja, which I will ask you about later in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, could you approximate for us, in addition to the 45 men that left Erdut, how many locals joined at Popovi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: At least ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you arrived in the -- in the town of Bijeljina and got off the bus, can you describe what happened when you got off the bus.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: We were told that terrorists in Bijeljina who were ethnic Muslims were supposed to be found by us and possibly liquidated. We were divided up into smaller groups in order to cover the entire town as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How many were in the group that you were subdivided into?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry to the usher: We're finished with that exhibit. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five, plus a local Serb who would show us the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that we briefly go into closed session for the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, can you continue and tell us the path that your group -- or what did your group do at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: My group and two other groups, we went in the direction of the bus station, and we occupied it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately what time of the day are we talking about now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Between 5.00 and 5.30 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you approximate the distance between where you got off the bus and where the bus station was? How far did your group have to travel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Well, we ran for about ten minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Between the time you left the bus and the time you arrived at the bus station, did you come under fire or meet any resistance to your entry into the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Not my group.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you observe when you arrived at the bus station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Can you clarify that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see any civilians on the streets of Bijeljina when you were making your way to the bus station or at the bus station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Well, after we had occupied the station, of course there were civilians who were going out to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did your group do with respect to those civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: We stopped civilians, and we put them into the waiting-room of the bus station in order to protect them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how many civilians were gathered into the bus station in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Ten to 15 at the time when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was the bus station in Bijeljina, was it located in the centre of the town or in the outskirts of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Well, say about 200 metres away from the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you observed a civilian being shot and killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. It was a civilian who didn't want to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe your observations regarding that incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Well, my fellow combatants stopped all civilians. This particular civilian didn't want to stop at the moment when he was being stopped. As far as I managed to gather later, he had been a retarded person. They shot at him because they thought he was trying to run away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was the man armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No, as far as we managed to find out later, but he kept his hand in his pocket. However, he had had physical problems with that hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you later learn the ethnicity of this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Around this time period, did members of the unit or the group that you were with fire upon a business establishment, a cafe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. Our superior officer shot from a hand-held launcher at a Muslim cafe called Cafe Istanbul.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where was this Cafe Istanbul located in relation to the bus station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: On the other side of the road, or about 15 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The transcript reads that you've described a hand-held launcher being used to fire upon the Cafe Istanbul. Were these the hand-held rocket launchers that you described were issued to the men prior to leaving Erdut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. That's the weapons that we were issued before leaving Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How many rockets altogether were fired into the Cafe Istanbul?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Five to seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask for a brief private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, what happened after this attack on the Cafe Istanbul?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: We were supposed to advance further, towards the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After arriving here in The Hague, were you asked to look at a videotape that depicted or depicts the Cafe Istanbul?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you look at a video clip now, and I then will ask you a few questions after it. It's approximately 40 seconds of video.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask if that could be set up for the witness, and when the director is ready, if he would please play it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] One of our wounded was here. It was horrible. You'll see a bit later that all the pipes were bullet-riddled.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We can stop the video now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, the white building on the corner, do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. That is the Cafe Istanbul.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened after the attack on the Cafe Istanbul? What did you and your portion of the group do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: We set out, passing the hotel, towards the park.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what happened when you entered the park?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I have to say first and foremost that I'm not sure whether we entered the park on the first day of the attack or the second day of the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The events that you've described up until this point, are you certain that those events occurred on the first day of the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the events in the park, you're not certain whether it's the first day or the second day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please continue with what happened in the park.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Just as we entered the park, shooting could be heard in town. We noticed, among other things, that we were being shot at. We also noticed that somebody was shooting at us from the water tower. Perhaps an hour later, this stopped. We passed through the park, and we reached a house. We spent some time in the house until the gunfire abated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Then the road to the hospital was practically free. We occupied the hospital. We searched it, and we placed our guards there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time on the first day when members of Arkan's unit took possession of cars belonging to some individuals in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many vehicles in all were taken that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: About 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did those vehicles that were taken that day include a bus as well as a new fire engine that belonged to the town of Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: From where were most of these vehicles taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Most of the cars were taken from in front of the house of a rich Muslim who was involved in repairing vehicles. However, he was not present. He had gone to Germany two days prior to the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was your unit directed to that house by any particular person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No, nobody directed our unit. However, the house was nearby, and it was sort of on the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At the time the vehicles were taken, was it known the ethnicity of the owner of that house and establishment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I myself did not know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you aware that other members of your unit did know the ethnicity of that man at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Perhaps only officers, because a civilian was with them, an ethnic Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of the man who had all of these vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened to these 40 vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: The same evening, they were taken in the direction of Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did they travel together or individually back to Erdut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Together, excluding the fire engine, which remained behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the path that was taken from Bijeljina back to Erdut in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Along the route depicted on the map that we looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The people who drove back to Erdut, were they only Arkan's Tigers or did they include some of the locals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Arkan's Tigers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In addition to the vehicles, was there any other property taken and transported back to Erdut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: In the same house where the vehicles were found, several cartons of cigarettes were found too, as well as detergent and some technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You mentioned -- you mentioned going to the hospital. Are you certain whether you went to the hospital on the first day or second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I'm certain that it was either on the first day or the second day, but I think it was on the second day, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe what, if anything, was the conditions at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: The conditions were quite normal. People were working normally. We had two wounded men, though. I don't know whether there were any other wounded persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you aware of there being casualties in addition to the two wounded men that were members of Arkan's Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: At that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you later learn how many casualties there were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, I did, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was that approximate number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Around 45.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've described an incident in the park during which you believed that you were being fired upon. Prior to that event, did you believe that you were under attack or meeting resistance before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No, not I myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to approximate for us how long it took Arkan's Tigers plus the local men that were with the group to secure the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: From six to eight hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that we go into private session for the remainder of this morning's session because I'm going to ask some questions that would reveal the identity of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll go into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand the equipment won't be available this morning. There's a possibility of some equipment being available at 5.00 this afternoon or 4.00 or tomorrow. I haven't recently been able to contact the witness to find out how he would feel about giving evidence at either of those times. I gather --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me interrupt to say that we -- we had notice of the possibility of an evening sitting. One of our number can't make it anyway, has his own arrangements, so that's not on even if it were practical, which I rather doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the witness, who is being extremely cooperative, whether there's any possibility of his travelling the shorter distance to Sarajevo. I don't know whether there is or not. I assume the answer will be negative. At least I'll ask that question. And I think I'd better liaise with Registry and your staff about re-ordering the witnesses for the rest of the week. If Sarajevo is possible tomorrow for that particular witness and this witness can be taken by some system on Wednesday, that might be an alternative. Wait and see, I think. Though it sounds as though definitely not today. As to the balance of the time that would be available to us this morning, I gather this witness will take in chief a little -- another 20 minutes or thereabouts. That would actually leave some time at the end of the day. The only other witness who might be called isn't really ready. I've made preparations, but I think it would probably be unfair on the witness to have him called today. In any event, he may have a medical appointment that he has to keep today, arising from a condition he suffers. So it looks as though there may be a gap today or in any event what would have been a gap but for the fact that we allow the evidence to spread into it. Not very satisfactory but I'm afraid nothing we can do about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, are you in a position to cross-examine this witness today or would you ask us to put that cross-examination back?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will cross-examine him, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, that would take up the balance probably, at least most of the day. I don't know if there are any administrative matters that we could deal with apart from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Leave me to work it out with Registry for the balance of the day and I'll report back at the end of the day, if I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Report back at the next break and we'll see how we're getting on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next break, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll see how we go from there. Yes. Let's have the witness back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to begin my next series of questions by asking you to look at a photograph. It will be displayed on the TV monitor in front of you. And if I could draw the rest of the Chamber's attention to Prosecution Exhibit 411, tab 6. Sir, I want you to focus on the man standing on the right-hand side of the photograph, and my question to you is: Do you recognise the uniform that that man is wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: The uniform belongs to Arkan's Guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recognise the item that is strapped across his back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. That's a hand-held rocket launcher of the Zolja type.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you recognise the weapon in his right hand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: An automatic rifle manufactured in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There is something black under his epaulette on the right-hand side. Do you recognise what that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: It's a cap, the so-called mask.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Other than the items that you've described, you were not present when this photograph was taken or recognise anything else in it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to an event. Did there come a time when you were travelling as a member of Arkan's unit to Erdut when you were stopped in Serbia by a member or members of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, about 15 days after the Bijeljina operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that we go into private session for the remainder of this portion of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, to draw you back to Bijeljina, did there come a time early in April when you learnt that some of the men from Arkan's unit that had been involved in Bijeljina went somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. Part of the group went to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After Bijeljina had been secured, was there discussion among Arkan's group with respect to a village called Janja, a Muslim village called Janja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was -- can you describe in substance what was the discussion regarding that village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: The discussion was that the inhabitants of Janja didn't want to go to war, but they handed over their weapons of their own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just drawing your attention once again to the group that went to Zvornik. Were you aware of what the purpose of them travelling to Zvornik was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I did not know, but I believe it was the same as in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At some point, were the mosques in Bijeljina destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was that during or after the town had been secured by Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 411, and that is tab 8, and I'd ask that it be placed on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to look at the exhibit that's on the projector on the platform to your left. Do you recognise what that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. It's a map of part of Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I could ask the director to focus on the map. If the director could please put on the overhead projector. It seems we are experiencing some technical difficulty. There is a map on the overhead projector, the ELMO. If we could have a view of that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, can you describe for us what is this map? Who drew this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: This is part of Bijeljina, and I drew the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does it involve some of the locations you've testified regarding this morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: It shows almost all the localities that I discussed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to now just point to the different locations that you've marked on the map that are relevant to your testimony here this morning. Please use the pointer. And you can look at the map as you point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: We reached -- we came in on this road, from the direction of the Popovi village. And in this area here, we had to go on foot up to the bus station. When we occupied the bus station, we shot at the Istanbul cafe. After all this, we continued along this route which took us by the hotel, through this park here, and there was shooting from the water tower here at us. And this here is a house in which we spent about an hour until the shooting died down, and then we continued along our route towards the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, on this map is there an indication of the house where the 40 cars were taken from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: The house is located here, behind the hotel?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm finished with that document. I'm going to ask now that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 411, tab 7. I'd ask that the witness be given the Serbo-Croatian original of this report, and the relevant portion will be displayed on the TV monitors in English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly request that the witness speak up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, in a little bit louder voice, could you please tell us, have you seen the document before you? Have you seen it before today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I saw it two or three days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does it report on some of the events -- or does it concern some events in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: It does not concern the events in the war, but it does concern certain things which the police undertook in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you in a position to have some personal knowledge about some of the activities that the police undertook and some of the observations they make contained in this report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I only know that checkpoints were set up at the exits to the towns and that a curfew was introduced which lasted the whole night.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As you read that report, was there anything that you noticed that was inaccurate, that you had personal knowledge was incorrect regarding what the report says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Around April of 1992, was there another paramilitary group established called the Serbian National Guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us, who was the person who established that organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Ljubisa Savic, nicknamed Mauzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at the screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be tab 4 of Prosecution 411. It was unavailable this morning. I will provide a copy to the Chamber later today, but it will appear on the screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to look at the screen in front of you. Do you recognise who is depicted in this still taken from a video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. That's the man nicknamed Mauzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did a number of men from Arkan's Tigers transfer from Arkan's Tigers over to Mauzer's Panthers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I now ask that we go into private session for the remaining questions I have for this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We missed that. There was no microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were born and you lived in Croatia, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Could you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: From the information I have, I have gathered that you are a Serb from Croatia. You were born in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You lived in a small town which, during the time of these events, was not within the framework of the Republic of Serbian Krajina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of this period that you are testifying about, you said that you needed to join the newly formed Croatian army; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: However, I gathered that you had some rather unpleasant experiences in that town in the course of the month of September 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: And also in May and in September.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. From May to September 1991.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: In May and in September. In the meantime, I was in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. You went to stay with relatives; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in May, because of the unpleasantness you experienced, you left the town, and then in September you returned and you came across the same kind of problems; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But earlier on, as I was able to gather, you were mistreated by people of your own age simply because you were a Serb, and they were reproaching you for being a fan of the Red Star club; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But the Red Star was a football club that was the Yugoslav champion, even a world champion for a period.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 2, second paragraph, you even say that you were attacked by a group of Croatian youths and that you were exposed to various threats simply because you were a Serb; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I was attacked in May.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And as far as I was able to gather from what you have said, you reduced your contacts mainly to other Serbs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that out of fear and because of the threats made against you and because of various actions by extremists in your town you decided to join the army in your town? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: However, when I say "the army," I'm referring to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: However, when you went to the barracks in September 1991, you were first arrested; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then in your town, you were in the army, nevertheless, for a while, because in the examination-in-chief, you put it slightly differently than is stated here in your statement, so I didn't quite understand. I won't read the name of the town. "I decided to join the JNA in ..." that town of yours it says here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And since they took you into custody first and checked out what was going on, and then on -- in paragraph 3 on page 2, you say you were admitted into the army. That is what is stated in your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. They admitted me to join them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So I understand you were admitted in the army. If not, in what capacity were you there if you were not a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: They issued me a weapon and a uniform, but they didn't register my existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that? How could they have issued you a weapon and uniform without taking your name down? Why would the army do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: They drafted a military booklet for me which to some extent confirmed that I was employed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean? What, did it confirm, to what extent, that you were employed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In what capacity were you employed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: As a non-commissioned officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. So you were a member of the army if you were a non-commissioned officer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Possibly. That military booklet was irregular.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Why was it irregular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Because I hadn't done my military service at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you could have joined the army as a volunteer. That is how you serve. You serve in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's not waste time on that any more. It wasn't clear to me whether you had been or not a member of the army. You obviously were. Now tell me very precisely, please, is it true that that barracks was attacked by Croatian paramilitary forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes; on three occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: During those three occasions during the two months that you were in that barracks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And when you left then, virtually the entire JNA staff who had been in the barracks left the barracks. So you left the barracks together with all the other members of the JNA that you found there and that abandoned the barracks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the first time they attacked you with sidearms only but that later on the attack was with tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: The first time with sidearms; the second time a police vehicle with, I assume, an anti-aircraft gun attacked us; and the third time, the army troops with tanks that had arrived from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They surrounded the barracks then, and then the negotiations took place for you to withdraw, to pull out from there but that you had to leave your weapons there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. We had nothing to defend ourselves with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, for how long you were under a blockade until the agreement was reached for you to pull out and to leave your weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Throughout that two-month period that I was there, electricity was cut. There was no water supply or food supplies could not be brought in. And I think that the telephone lines were also cut but I'm not so sure about that. There were radio communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you left a barracks that was surrounded and under a blockade for a whole of two months until you pulled out of the barracks and left your weapons; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: It wasn't surrounded for all of two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But it was blocked for two months.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I gathered that upon leaving the barracks something unpleasant occurred, that is, they put a pistol in your mouth and threatened to kill you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But then their officer said that the agreement was that all of you should leave the barracks alive, and then they let you go too, as they did the other JNA members; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Or, rather, they allowed you to pull out of the barracks unhindered.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: We were escorted by the Croatian police up until the exit from the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since you were the -- a local inhabitant of that town, they threatened to kill you if you ever returned to that town; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is the reason for your fleeing Croatia fear and the threat that you received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And as far as I understand it from your statement, because of this fear and the fact that you had to move out, you decided to enlist with the Serbian volunteer guards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, because I could not enjoy the status of refugee in Serbia. They wanted to send me back with the army to the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So were you a deserter for the JNA at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At one point during your examination-in-chief, you mentioned, according to my notes, that you were being looked for by the military police of Serbia, as you put it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. In the Red Cross, I was told that I had to register with the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you mentioned the military police of Serbia. You know that Serbia didn't have a military police as it didn't have an army. It could only have been the military police of the JNA. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But the event occurred in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You were being looked for by the military police because you were a member of the JNA when you withdrew from the town that you withdrew from. Very well. So your joining the Serbian Volunteer Guard, and your later involvement in operations, so your participation in the war was exclusively based on your personal decision; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 18061 to 18069.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were you armed and did you join that combat unit prompted by personal motives and not by any other outside influence or pressure or for any other reason? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: When I was -- when I applied, I was prompted by personal motives. Later on, I was bound by contract.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understand, you signed that contract again on the basis of your own personal decision.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And I also gathered that you then went to Erdut for training; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The same day that you enlisted, signed the contract, you went to Erdut.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived at Erdut for training, were you aware of the fact that this Serbian Volunteer Guard headed by Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, was a part of the army of SAO Krajina, which later became the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the people you found in Erdut and with whom you trained, were they mostly, like you, from the territory of Croatia, that is, nationals of Croatia? I see some nicknames like Osijek and the like. Yes or no. You speak about that on page 4, second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. There were various rumours about that unit, that is the Serbian Volunteer Guards. Is it true that very strict discipline prevailed and there were heavy -- heavy punishment for the slightest offence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you exercised very heavily, that you ran a distance of 25 kilometres one day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that while you were in Erdut and the surrounding villages, Dalj, or anywhere in that area, had you heard that any local from those villages had gone missing or had been killed or had -- a crime had been committed against them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: While I was there, I had no knowledge of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know of any crime committed by your colleague within that unit of which you were a member, the Serbian Volunteer Guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: You mean in that area?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I mean generally, because you say that you were a member of the Serbian volunteer guards. Do you have any knowledge that any one of your colleagues committed a crime that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Only from rumours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, since you're testifying about 45 of you going to Bijeljina, is it true that you went to Bijeljina having been asked to come there by the local authorities, the local authorities of Bijeljina or the broader area around it? I don't know exactly. But my point in asking you this question is whether you went there upon the invitation of the local authorities.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: I don't know that much. I know from later stories that Mauzer had called Arkan to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'll read out to you the reason for us being there was, and this is the one but last paragraph on page 5 of your statement, that: "Ljubisa Savic, known as Mauzer, asked for aid on behalf of the local Serbs from Bijeljina, and there was even some sort of an arrangement mentioning a certain sum of money." That is what is stated in your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, but I cannot guarantee that that was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But you had also heard, what is contained in your statement, that some money was mentioned, money that was received for this activity.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So according to your knowledge, this group of yours went within the scope of a private arrangement made with the local authorities in Bijeljina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Possibly. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, please, did you have anything to do with the JNA or the police of the Republic of Serbia or any kind of links did that unit have with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Not when we're talking about the attack on Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that this Mauzer was an official of the democratic party? That's the one that's in power now in Serbia. He was not even an official of Karadzic's Serb Democratic Party. He was an official of the Democratic Party for Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: After awhile, you went to Popovi, and that is where you and your colleagues from the unit played the role of instructors; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: No, not in Popovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this because in the last paragraph of this statement of yours, you say: "Then we went to Popovi, and we encountered Serbs who were being trained by our men. And then they divided us up into nine groups of five men respectively, and in every group there was a local Serb so they could take us around," et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1738
utterances.text: Yes. This sentence refers to our actual arrival in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Your actual arrival in Bijeljina, not this training. All right. Let me just take a look.
